body: Nifty ~12,430 (Jan 2020 high; 12,168 cited as the pre-crash reference) to 7,511 on 24 Mar 2020, about -38 to -40%; Sensex ~42,270 to ~25,640 (levels from memory). Nifty 50 TRI -38% vs Smallcap 250 TRI -43% (DSP); Smallcap 100 intra-year fall -47%. Market cap/GDP fell to ~56% in March 2020 (Business Standard; other estimates ~70% on FY20 GDP) - the lowest in a decade. Recovery: the Nifty regained its high in Nov 2020 (about 8-10 months; sources differ on day counts), doubled to 15,000 by Feb 2021, and the Smallcap 100 was up 141% from its March low by the end of FY21. Bottom signals: global central-bank 'whatever it takes' (Fed unlimited QE 23 Mar 2020; RBI's 75bp cut on 27 Mar), valuation near decade lows, forced selling and record pessimism, a surge in new retail demat accounts. Leaders of the recovery: pharma, IT, specialty chemicals, metals, then small caps broadly; laggards: banks (loan moratorium), hotels, aviation. Rs 1 lakh in Smallcap 250 TRI at the Mar 2020 bottom became ~Rs 5 lakh by Mar 2026 (~31% CAGR) vs ~Rs 2.9 lakh (~19%) if invested in Jan 2020 (DSP). Lesson: exogenous crashes met by massive liquidity recover fastest; the best entries came when valuation indicators (mcap/GDP <60-70%) and policy turned together.
title: COVID crash and liquidity recovery (2020-21)
